Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're targeting the first production sync in early December and need to confirm the access-control sequencing for SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and the network/IP policy. High level:

- We require SAML SSO integration with our IdP (Okta). We'll share metadata but want to confirm Redwood's EntityID, ACS URL, and any constraints on NameID format.
- SCIM provisioning: we plan to push groups + title/titlecode attributes. We need to know required/optional SCIM attributes, provisioning cadence (near-real time vs nightly), and the expected service account scopes.
- IP allowlist / firewall: we'll provide a limited set of egress IPs from our VPC; please confirm the Redwood inbound ranges we need to whitelist.
- Service account: request a dedicated service account for user sync with key rotation policy details.
- Compliance: our security team will request evidence that SCIM syncs are logged and that service account keys are auditable for SOC2.

Attached is our initial requirements spreadsheet (clearline_sso_requirements.xlsx). Can we get a short plan + proposed sequencing and a suggested maintenance window so we can coordinate?

Thanks,

Hi Daniel — great to meet you over email.

Thanks for the spreadsheet; that helps. Attached is our recommended implementation playbook (redwood_onboard_mop.pdf) and a short checklist specific to SAML/SCIM sequencing. Summary and proposed sequencing below (high level):

1) Discovery (this week) — confirm IdP metadata (EntityID, ACS URL, cert thumbprint), SCIM attribute map, and confirm exact IP ranges you will whitelist.
2) Staging integration (week of 2026-11-22) — we’ll exchange metadata and provision a staging tenant + a sandbox service account for SCIM. Jonas will run an initial provisioning dry-run.
3) Validation & security review (2026-11-29 to 2026-12-02) — run full sync in staging, review audit logs and key rotation workflow with your SecOps.
4) Production cutover (target 2026-12-05 during proposed maintenance window 02:00–04:00 PT) — final metadata swap, rotate keys, enable SCIM provisioning to prod.

Open asks for your team:
- Can you send the Okta metadata XML and confirm NameID format preference?
- Confirm the SCIM attribute list you expect to provision (please highlight required fields).
- Confirm IP ranges to add to your allowlist and whether you manage TLS inspection in front of the IdP.

Jonas and Monica are looped in for the engineering handoff — Monica will own the SCIM mapping and provisioning cadence, Jonas will own network/IP reachability and service-account policy. I'll coordinate the security artifacts for SOC2.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Marissa / Jonas — quick internal note on the technical checklist (we'll paste relevant parts to the customer but want to align first):

- SCIM mapping: we support users -> {userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work], active, title, groups}. Additional custom attributes (e.g., titlecode) can be mapped as custom schema but require a field mapping doc and a staging dry-run.
- Provisioning cadence options: near-real-time (SCIM push via events) or scheduled (poll every 5–15 minutes). For enterprise customers we usually recommend poll-5 for minimal throttling risk but event-driven for low-latency workflows.
- Service account scopes: provisioning service account should have /scim.write and /audit.read scopes. Keys are rotated every 90 days by default; we can set a stricter policy on request.
- Audit evidence: we maintain request/response logs for SCIM operations (retention: 90 days standard, extendable). For SOC2 we can produce the provisioning audit export and a key-rotation log.

Action items for engineering:
- Jonas: validate IP ranges and confirm which public egress addresses we will expose for Clearline's allowlist. I can produce the initial mapping doc and run the staging sync once we have Okta XML.
- Marissa: confirm the AUP and who will sign the service-account agreement (DocuSign link).

I updated the internal runbook and added a stub template for the service-account description (service_account_template.txt).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
